@StanleyShih8 I think almost everything about my $AXTI thesis from 2025 was validated? 

From AXT's position in the InP substrate bottleneck... Being able to threaten the hyperscaler buildout (per Reuters)... 

$IQE has been flagging this as a major risk, VPEC and Taiwan epiwafer foundries have been crying over InP substrate bottlenecks. 

And there's even AXT direct confirmation of partnerships with $LITE and $COHR as the InP substrate supplier. AXT also stated $130m/quarter InP revenue capacity exiting 2027 (~$520m annualized) so that's a massive revenue inflection compared to previously. 

Now... the biggest question is: How much can AXT price hike? 

The substrates they make are just such a tiny part of the BOM... but can threaten hyperscaler buildouts with optics. 

So if they manage to price hike to $SNDK NAND degrees (which they can), then I think AXT could get re-rated a ton from here. But if they end up like Japanese ABF suppliers that are less willing to abuse their position, that's a different story.  

Will need to do more channel checks to see how that's coming along.

But at the very least, I would argue there should be some valuation baseline just due to their critical importance (eg. upstream refinery ownerships, crucible processing, etc) + existing capacity revenue without hikes. 

TLDR: 
- Bottleneck thesis was at like ~$500m MC 
- Upside now comes from price hikes due to duopoly position + ownership of upstream bottlenecks in the InP substrate manufacturing process. (which they can due to low cost of InP substrates in overall costs) 
- Uncharted territory, we'll see (also a central part of geopolitical tensions so there's always risk there).

@Rian_2026 Good question! Just some informal thoughts... there's three "moats" to look at for $SIVE:

- Capacity 
- Qualifications (especially for custom DFB lasers)
- Technological

1. For capacity, they're coming online with 100M+ CW DFB lasers Q4 2027 (global supply is roughly ~608M EML/CW lasers currently per Trendforce). 

Obviously by 2027 global capacity is going to grow a lot, with $AAOI, $AVGO (3x expansion), and others coming online.  

But if you extrapolate their 2:1 statement, that implies 300m lasers/year long term coming from their own supply + external foundries. 

This is incredibly valuable during a shortage that was quoted to be 3-5 years, and $LITE stating they already have demand visibility into 2031...

And when suppliers have started to qualify many more (eg. 5-7 vendors vs. 2-3 earlier) due to bottlenecks. 

I'm sure a lot of how they achieve that staggering amount is due to their manufacturing process/yields (which is a moat). 

2. For qualifications, if you look at 70mW/100mW pluggable lines with Chinese players, I'd argue this is more generic and moreso reverting back to a capacity  argument and manufacturing process to achieve those numbers. 

Custom DFB arrays that they've been working on with Ayar (they hinted at 2-3 others back in 2023 like Celestial) take years for optical i/o related things and would be a moat if they finish quals. 

So it's not quite something you can hot swap or design out really easily for $MTSI or another company. But of course cpo scale up and such is mass volume in 2028, and we're still H2 2026. 

3. People can always compare raw specs like power output, but it's probably way way more nuanced so easier to just point toward customer statements. 

With $JBL 1.6T LRO: "I think that there's the potential for a relatively dramatic moat with our LRO part…" from Jabil's EVP, especially related to power consumption. And $SIVE is my guess sole source in this line. 

Jabil is probably the most important testament to how their lasers perform in mass production scenarios maybe around Q2 next year. 

Ayar said something similar along the lines of "we couldn't do it without Sivers" for custom implementations.

$NBIS

Not all neoclouds are created the same way not all neocloud capacity is worth the same, and this chart shows it.

Every gigawatt Nebius signs away in a long-term hosting deal brings in roughly $20-25B. 

The same gigawatt sold short-term on its own platform brings in $40-50B. Same power, same data center, about double the revenue.

Serverless inference is the purest version of that. 

Instead of renting a cluster for five years, customers pay per token for exactly what they use, while Nebius runs the hardware, the software and the optimization in between.

Why I think it's the next big leg for $NBIS:

+ Training is lumpy and driven by a few giant customers. Inference is every company shipping an AI product, every single day.
+ Usage-based pricing scales with adoption. More agents means more tokens, which means more revenue from the same gigawatt.
+ The software is the moat. Uptime guarantees, speculative decoding and auto-scaling are hard to copy for someone who's just renting out racks.
+ It spreads revenue across thousands of customers instead of a couple of hyperscalers.

The big contracts pay for the build but inference is where the money is.

Bet on the companies that are pushing for more server-less inference.

For me, that’s $NBIS

Interconnect is the fastest-growing part of the stack. 

AI networking grows 43% a year to ~$394B, AI switching 51%, and optical reaches $111B. Co-packaged optics goes from basically zero to $14B by 2030.

AI CPUs for agentic workloads grow from $18.5B to $180B, a 44% CAGR.

Every AI layer on this table compounds three to four times faster.

这次 FOMC，我更愿意准备的交易，是加息兑现后利率压力缓和、黄金重新走强。前提是债券市场先给确认。

本周周报里，我的基准已经写得很清楚：加息 25bp，随后观察。十二月再加一次需要防范，但我还没有足够证据把持续加息作为基准。到了会议前，市场对这次加息已经给出接近九成的定价。继续押注加息本身，能赚到的预期差已经有限；后面有没有更多紧缩，才决定这笔交易还能走多远。

这也是我认为今晚最容易被忽略的地方：美联储加息，债券完全可以上涨。如果市场此前一直担心联储落后于通胀，愿意采取行动，反而可能缓解长端债券要求的通胀风险补偿。与此同时，只要点阵图和记者会没有把未来利率推到市场已经计入的路径之上，前端紧缩预期也有回吐空间。两条逻辑可以同时发生，但必须分别验证，不能看见 10Y 下来，就宣布市场开始交易降息。

2004 年开始加息后，长端收益率仍曾持续下降；2015 年首次加息后的次年，也出现过明显的美债上涨。这些历史提醒我，政策利率与市场利率有不同的节奏。它们不能证明今晚一定见顶，更不能把几个月的行情压缩成凌晨两点的一根 K 线。当时的增长、通胀和资金流背景也各不相同。

我今晚要观察的是：联储正式兑现紧缩之后，市场还愿不愿意继续卖债。

点阵图上，今年年底的 3.9% 和 4.1% 是两个直观的观察位置。如果本次加息到 3.75%—4.00%，年底中位数约 3.9%，就对应年内不再净加息；约 4.1%，则对应还有一次 25bp。但市场已经在防第二次加息，所以 4.1% 不能自动等同于超预期鹰派。我更关心 2027 年那一列，未来的降息空间有没有继续被拿掉，以及记者会是否支持市场把高利率维持时间再往后推。

真正可能形成 pain trade 的情景，是加息落地，后续路径却没有市场担心的那么高，收益率冲高之后反而回落。届时，提前按更高利率做出的空头和对冲就可能需要调整。这里我押注的是预期差，至于会不会演变成挤仓，要由价格证明，不能把高加息概率直接当成空头仓位拥挤的证据。

不过，联储能影响通胀预期，解决不了原油供应。 这也是我不会仅凭一次加息就重仓押注利率见顶的原因。只要油价、燃料成本继续上行，市场仍可能提高对通胀持续性的判断。更舒服的组合，是联储兑现紧缩后债券不再跌，随后原油也开始突破失败。政策信誉改善与能源压力缓和同时出现，利率回落才更容易延续。

这条路径里，我优先盯黄金。我需要看到美元和实际利率停止抬高，黄金面对加息消息不再创新低，随后收回会前整理区间，回踩仍有承接。只有名义收益率下降还不够：如果通胀预期下降得更快，实际利率仍可能上升，黄金也未必得到支持。

交易上，我会先用 GLD 或有明确最大亏损的 call spread，做未来 1—10 个交易日的修复。确认后的回踩是入场观察点，第一目标看前期整理区间上沿，再看前高；如果重新跌破确认低点，就退出。没有确认，仓位就是零。这里不需要提前梭哈，也不需要猜中记者会里的每一个形容词。

股票端，也不要因为加息就追空。利率压力缓和、信用保持稳定，足以给 QQQ、地产和部分融资敏感板块带来反弹。但我对 AI 资本回报的怀疑不会因此消失，产业逻辑可以偏空，短线仍要尊重利率回落带来的反弹；利空落地却跌不动时，已有空头要先重新评估风险。

让我认错的条件也很明确：点阵图和记者会继续推动市场上修利率路径，2Y 与 10Y 实际收益率持续走高，美元走强，黄金确认低点失守；或者油价继续突破，信用开始恶化。出现这些信号，我会撤掉“利率压力缓和”的交易，不拿历史类比给亏损做心理按摩。

我的基准仍然是一次加息、随后观察。今晚如果加息之后债券不再跌、黄金不再跌，我会认真对待这个信号。真正的仓位，等记者会后价格站稳再加。

With BOTH the 10-year yields and the U.S. dollar rising, here is how to plan for the worst-case scenario. I've experienced this market scenario already in my life.

Markets kept making all-time highs for 4 - 5 months, and then a -57% crash happened in the markets. But rising yields and dollar rising does NOT crash the markets alone. Something UNDERNEATH is typically the trigger.

The 2026 - 2027 triggers would be:

1. Private credit - this is the scarier one in my opinion. Seven major platforms (Blue Owl, Apollo, Ares, BlackRock, and Blackstone) have capped or blocked investor withdrawals. $4.6 billion is trapped basically. 

2. Auto loan delinquencies hit a record - 5.5% at 90+ days, worse than 2008 peak (5.3%). The consumer is cracking at the bottom.

3. Commercial real estate is at record deliquicieis - office CMBS delinquiency at 12.3%, higher than 2008 crisis. 

4. Corporate bankruptcies at 16 year highs - 372 large filings through mid-2026. Small business bankrupties up 50% as well.

5. S&P 500 is looking a lie right now - every sector fell in Sept except for tech - banks, utilities, equal weight S&P 500, only a few BIG tech names are holding up the markets 

6. Six banks have failed in 2026 - small ones, but the most in any year this decade. 

I find that the pattern is the same throughout our history; rates stay high, something that was relying on cheap money can't handle it, then that thing breaks, the break spreads to other things, and by the time the Fed cuts rates to fix it, the damage is already done.

So how do you prepare for this since we cannot TIME a top?

1. Raise cash gradually - don't sell everything. Don't go all-in on a few names. Raise cash from work and you'll have the opportunity of a life time waiting for you when the dip comes

2. Buy the 10 year - a 5.35% risk free yield is the highest in 24 years. You can park cash in short term Treasuries (SHV, BIL, SGOV) and get paid 5%+ while you wait. My wife and I have started buying 10 year as well.

3. Watch the leaders, not the index - the S&P is being held up by 5-7 names. When $NVDA, $AAPL, $MSFT start breaking lower on volume, that's your signal the last pillar is cracking. The rest of the market is already weak.

4. Avoid the junk, or size appropriately - small caps, unprofitable tech, high debt companies, anything that needs to refinance soon. The Russell 2000 has a third of its constituents classified as zombie companies. These get destroyed when credit tightens.

5. Quality over momentum - if you're staying long, own companies with no debt, strong cash flow, and pricing power. Think $GOOGL, $AMGN, $BRK. Companies that don't need to borrow money at 5%+ don't care about rates.

6. Don't short the top - the market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent. In 2007 the S&P rallied 5% for 4 months after the 10Y peaked. Being early on a short is the same as being wrong. Can hedge with defensives instead and/or raise cash.

7. Have a plan before you need one - decide now what you'll do if the S&P drops 10%, 20%, 30%. Write it down. When panic hits, you execute the plan instead of making emotional decisions.

The goal isn't to predict the crash. It's to survive it with enough capital to buy the bottom and become a multi-millionaire.

英伟达 10-K 里有个数字我觉得一直被低估：员工流失率 2% 出头，全科技行业最低的那一档。三万多人的公司，2020 年初进去那批，当年一个三十万美金的四年 RSU 包，拿到今天是千万级别。

正常公司靠还没 vest 的股票锁人。这批人早就不缺钱了，真正按住他们的是那根还在往上走的线——「明年还能再翻一倍」这个念头，比任何合同都管用。

所以它都不用跌。横一年就够了，三万多个已经财务自由的人会同时想起来：我可以去创业、可以去 OpenAI、也可以回家躺着🌚 假设你是 Jensen，手上唯一的留人工具就是那张图。 $NVDA

Jensen owns roughly 3.5% of Nvidia and gets roughly 3.5% of the votes. No founder class, no Class B, nothing — one share one vote, same as you.

Then look at the people buying his chips. Zuck holds something like 13% of Meta's economics and ~61% of the votes. Page and Brin walked away from operating roles years ago and still sit on supervoting stock that effectively controls Alphabet. Musk spent two years saying out loud he wasn't going to build AI inside Tesla without ~25% voting control, and shareholders handed him a package engineered to walk him there.

So everyone on the demand side bolted the doors from the inside. The one company that actually has pricing power never bothered.

Say you're on Nvidia's board and you've decided Jensen has to go. Who are you calling to make the chips?

Everyone's waiting to see AI turn up in the electricity bill. It'll turn up in the price of a laptop first.

An HBM bit eats roughly three times the wafer capacity of a plain DRAM bit, and Hynix and Samsung have spent two years converting lines over to make them, so commodity DRAM supply has been shrinking right into the best demand year memory has ever had. You haven't felt it because PCs and phones buy on contract — that repricing lands a couple of quarters late, inside somebody's gross margin. Dell's, for one. Memory is a real chunk of the BOM there, the operating margin is mid single digits, and the guy outbidding them for the same wafer is financing his cluster with money that doesn't care what it costs. There isn't much of a negotiation in that.

Cleanest money in AI is still memory. Hynix helped build this shortage and is selling into it.

很多人对现在加州Santa Clara潜伏着多少靠打工财富自由的隐形富豪根本没概念。

就拿英伟达来说，除了日常发的期权，公司有个员工购股计划（ESPP），允许大家拿工资打八五折买自家的股票，每年IRS规定的认购上限是2.5万美元。

假设你是一个2014年入职的普通工程师，什么花里胡哨的波段都不做，只是每年死板地把这2.5万的额度拉满。十年下来，你用死工资投入了25万本金。

因为ESPP机制自带回溯低价再打折的优势，叠加上这十年英伟达离谱的暴涨和拆股，光是这一个不起眼的死工资定投账户，目前的市值都已经妥妥在千万美元以上。注意，这还没算那些真正占大头的RSU期权奖励。

假设你现在个人账户里趴着大几千万美元随时能套现的资产，每天开着车去园区打卡，看着旁边刚入职、为了年底几千块绩效卷生卷死的新同事，你猜自己面对屏幕上那些报错代码时是什么心态。

【美股复盘 · 10月9日】

大市方面，环球宏观消息聚焦于人工智能巨头营收表现及数据中心功耗瓶颈，惟相关扰动无碍美股三大指数全线造好，当中道指表现一枝独秀。全日市况靠稳，道指 ( $DIA ) 全日收报516.11点，升0.87%；标普 (SPY) 收报778.57点，升0.60%；纳指 (QQQ) 收报751.27点，升0.49%；反映中小型股走势的罗素小型股 (IWM) 亦收报278.93点，升0.49%。大市气氛正面，市宽表现强劲，观察名单内104只股份中，多达70只录得上升，仅34只下跌，买盘主导大市方向。

板块走势上，云端软件及网络安全类股份走强，带动科网板块整体气氛。Snowflake (SNOW) 抽升7.42%，Cloudflare (NET) 及 Palantir (PLTR) 分别急升5.57%及5.17%，网络安全概念股 Palo Alto Networks (PANW) 与 CrowdStrike (CRWD) 亦受资金追捧，录得逾4%至5%升幅；通讯设备股 Ciena (CIEN) 亦靠稳造好，升5.60%。反观半导体板块则领跌，受制于业界对高带宽内存(HBM)产能挤压普通内存之忧虑，以及晶圆代工巨头间的高阶设备资本博弈，半导体股普遍遇沽压，Arm (ARM) 挫3.27%，安森美半导体 (ON)、英特尔 (INTC) 与超微半导体 (AMD) 跌幅介乎2.03%至2.37%，板块走势反复偏软。

焦点个股中，莫德纳 (MRNA) 受资金热捧，全日暴涨14.21%，升幅冠绝观察名单。电动车巨头特斯拉 (TSLA) 将发布自动驾驶出租车Cybercab，华尔街正密切注视其首批测试车队注册数据能否重塑估值定锚，惟相关题材未见明显炒作。此外，受AI数据中心耗电及资本开支忧虑影响，超微电脑 (SMCI) 走势疲弱，跌2.14%；流媒体巨头奈飞 (NFLX) 亦挫1.77%。中概股阿里巴巴 (BABA) 则逆市发力，全日急升5.36%。太空概念股 AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) 遭遇庞大沽压，急泻10.48%，表现失守包尾。

小结而言，分析指目前华尔街资本正从大语言模型之纯估值炒作，逐步转向数据中心、电网等底层基建实物资产重新定锚，资金流向反映市场对科技巨头财务纪律及实质盈利转化之审视趋于严谨。后市料继续受制于大型科技股之资本开支节奏及宏观基本面，关键位将聚焦于重磅科技股能否守稳支持位，以及资金能否持续流入防守类及传统价值板块顶托大市。
